title: Enhancing Microservices Anomaly Detection via Multimodal Data Fusion in the Wavelet Domain and Spatiotemporal Graph-based Diffusion Probabilistic Model

problem.claim: Microservices complexity creates challenges for failure diagnosis.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal data mining insufficiently exploits cross-modal information and spatiotemporal associations.

contributions.claim: A multimodal anomaly-detection method transforms three modal data types into the wavelet domain and fuses them with attention.
A spatiotemporal-graph DDPM combines spatiotemporal learning and uncertainty measurement to generate future samples non-autoregressively for multi-horizon prediction.
The method is reported to improve anomaly-detection performance on three public datasets and one real-world production system.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the proposed anomaly-detection method and spatiotemporal-graph diffusion model as new.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments reportedly show significant anomaly-detection performance improvements on three public datasets and a real-world production system.
The authors report that multimodal fusion extracts information absent from the original modalities and enhances anomaly detection.

narrative_sequence.summary: Microservices complexity makes failure diagnosis challenging.
Prior multimodal mining does not fully exploit modality-specific information or spatiotemporal associations.
The paper proposes wavelet-domain attention fusion for three modal data types.
It adds a spatiotemporal-graph DDPM for non-autoregressive multi-horizon prediction with uncertainty measurement.
The authors report improved anomaly-detection performance across three public datasets and a production system.

source_observation.claim: Combining multimodal fusion with explicit frequency, temporal, and spatial modeling is presented as a way to address incomplete information use in anomaly detection.

interpretation.claim: Anomaly-detection systems may benefit when representation learning and dependency modeling target complementary dimensions of the data.

application.claim: For microservices observability, consider fusing heterogeneous signals while modeling their temporal evolution and service relationships.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond the reported datasets and production system.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three modal data types.
Dataset names, evaluation metrics, baselines, and numerical results are omitted.
Model architecture, training procedure, and computational requirements are unspecified.
The production-system setting and anomaly characteristics are not described.
